# XY Forever serial protocol 1.33: streamed reads and writes, file hashes

Part of the [XY Forever serial protocol 1.33](../PROTOCOL.md).

### 0x1a `file.write_begin`

Start a streamed, replace-safe write of one file. Opens the write window and creates `/yaffs2/xy-forever/tmp/put-<size>-<crc>` (8 lowercase hex digits each),
replacing a leftover of that name; the target is not touched. Any earlier streamed write is abandoned first (its temporary file removed). A job in progress is
`busy`. The bytes follow with `file.write_data`; `file.write_end` finishes. A write left without data for 5 s is abandoned the same way (a cut cable); temporary
files left by a power cut are removed when the USB service next starts.

| Request field (50 to 280 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | cstr UTF-8, 10..240 B | the file to create or replace, as for `file.write_staged`; missing folders are created |
| `size` | u32 | the file's size in bytes (0 allowed) |
| `crc` | u32 | CRC-32 of the whole file |
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | SHA-256 of the whole file: the confirmation `file.write_end` checks before the target changes |

Reply: the status only.

Errors: `bad_request`, `refused`, `busy`, `link`, `storage`. Tool timeout: 60 s. **Destructive**: ask the user first. Build switch `XYF_USB_FILE_WRITE`, not
optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since 1.18.

### 0x1b `file.write_data`

Send the next piece of a streamed write. As `stage.data`, but each piece goes to the temporary file at once: `range` when `offset` is not the bytes received so
far or the data would pass the announced size; a resend inside what was received is ok and `received` stays (its bytes are not compared: `file.write_end` checks
the file). `state` without a streamed write in progress. A failed storage write (`storage`, `link`; a full storage is `storage`) abandons the write and removes
the temporary file when it can.

| Request field (5 to 4160 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `offset` | u32 | must equal the bytes received so far |
| `data` | rest, 1..4156 B | the next bytes; send `put_chunk` (1024) at a time, or (1.33) `max_data` (4096) when `hello` says `pipe` is above 1; processor B writes them before it answers |

| Reply field, after the status (4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `received` | u32 | bytes received and written so far |

On an error: the status only. Errors: `state`, `range`, `link`, `storage`. Tool timeout: 30 s. Build switch `XYF_USB_FILE_WRITE`, not optional: the firmware
does not build without it. Since 1.18.

### 0x1c `file.write_end`

Check the streamed file and rename it onto its target. Closes the temporary file, checks the received bytes' CRC-32 and SHA-256 against `file.write_begin`
(`crc`, `sha`), reads the file back and compares its CRC-32 (`crc`), then processor A checks its size against its name and renames it onto the target in one
step (yaffs replaces an existing file atomically: after a power cut the target is the old file or the new one, never a partial one). A target that is a folder
is `storage` (error 21). On any failure the temporary file is removed and the target is unchanged. `state` when not every announced byte arrived or no streamed
write is in progress. The host waits 60 s plus 1 s per 20000 bytes.

Request: empty (the device ignores any payload).

| Reply field, after the status (12 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `written` | u32 | bytes written to the temporary file |
| `readback_crc` | u32 | CRC-32 of the temporary file read back (0 when it was not read) |
| `error` | u32 | the device file system's error number of the rename (0 when none; 21 the target is a folder) |

On an error: every field (zero where not reached). Errors: `state`, `crc`, `sha`, `link`, `storage`, `not_found`. Tool timeout: 120 s. **Destructive**: ask the
user first. Build switch `XYF_USB_FILE_WRITE`, not optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since 1.18.

### 0x1d `file.hash`

Hash a stored file on the device: its size and SHA-256. Reads the file to its end on the device, over the same storage requests `file.read` uses (4 KiB pieces),
and hashes it, so a tool can check a stored file without reading it back over USB (#327: a package's staged files before it is published). Paths and refusals as
`file.read`'s; a file over 64 MiB is `too_large`. Changes nothing. The host waits 60 s plus 1 s per 20000 bytes it expects.

| Request field (10 to 240 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | cstr UTF-8, 10..240 B | absolute path under `/yaffs2/`, NUL-terminated, as `file.read`'s |

| Reply field, after the status (36 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `size` | u32 | bytes read to the end of the file |
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | SHA-256 of those bytes |

On an error: the status only. Errors: `bad_request`, `refused`, `link`, `storage`, `not_found`, `too_large`. Tool timeout: 120 s. Build switch
`XYF_USB_FILE_WRITE`, not optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since 1.32.

### 0x1e `file.read_stream`

Read the next piece of a file, kept open between pieces. As a ranged `file.read`, for whole files: the device keeps the file open after a reply, and a request
for the same path at the offset where the last reply ended reads on from there (one storage request per piece, no open, seek or close). Any other request (path,
offset or command), or no request for 1 s, closes it first; a resend of an earlier piece opens the file again. To read a file, ask `max_data` bytes (or
`max_read` when `pipe` is 1) from offset 0 until a reply holds fewer, keeping up to `pipe` requests in flight. Reads only: the write window stays as it is.

| Request field (18 to 248 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | cstr UTF-8, 10..240 B | absolute path under `/yaffs2/`, NUL-terminated, as `file.read`'s |
| `offset` | u32 | first byte to read |
| `length` | u32 | bytes to read: at most `max_data` (4096) when `hello` says `pipe` is above 1, else at most `max_read` (1024) (1..4096) |

| Reply field, after the status (0 to 4096 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | rest, 0..4096 B | up to `length` bytes, fewer only at the end of the file |

On an error: the status only. Errors: `bad_request`, `refused`, `link`, `storage`, `not_found`, `range`. The reply never gains fields (it ends in `rest`). Tool
timeout: 15 s. Build switch `XYF_USB_FILE_WRITE`, not optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since 1.33.
